result.title: Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?
result.summary: A neural model is the set of functions that can be expressed by a given neural network architecture. Neural models contain natural submodels, such as those obtained by setting some neurons to be inactive. We study the geometry of neural models and ask whether they prefer their submodels. By this we mean whether local minimizers of the loss function lie in a given submodel. We introduce a geometric framework to determine if this occurs. For shallow multilayer perceptrons, we show that subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred. For deep multilayer perceptrons, we give conditions under which subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are not preferred. For lightning self-attention, lower-rank submodels are usually not preferred, but we identify examples where they are because they lie on a boundary of the model. Our results show that, aside from a few exceptions, preference for submodels cannot be explained by the geometry of the neural model, and must instead come from other sources such as training dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究神经网络"模型"（架构可表达的函数集合）的几何结构，提出一个几何框架来判断损失函数的局部极小点是否落在子模型内（如隐藏神经元失活、自注意力低秩子模型），并对浅层/深层 MLP 与 lightning self-attention 给出「不被偏好」的条件与边界反例，结论是子模型偏好大多需由训练动力学而非几何解释。
